objects.definition:
class UTILITE_EXPORT UEventsHandler : public UEventsSender {
public:

	void registerToEventsManager();
	void unregisterFromEventsManager();
    

protected:
    /**
     * Only the UEventsManager has access
     * to the handleEvent() method.
     */
    friend class UEventsManager;

    /**
     * Method called by the UEventsManager
     * to handle an event. Important : this method 
     * must do a minimum of work because the faster 
     * the dispatching loop is done; the faster the 
     * events are received. If a handling function 
     * takes too much time, the events list can grow 
     * faster than it is emptied. The event can be
     * modified.
     * @return "true" to notify UEventsManager that this handler took ownership of the
     *         event (meaning it must delete it). The event will
     *         not be dispatched to next handlers.
     * @return "false" to let event be dispatched to next handlers (default behavior). UEventsManager
     *         will take care of deleting the event.
     *
     */
    virtual bool handleEvent(UEvent * event) = 0;

protected:
    /**
     * UEventsHandler constructor.
     *
     * Note : You can call EventsManager::addHandler(this) at
     * the end of the constructor of the inherited class where the virtual
     * method handleEvent(...) is defined. If so, the UEventsHandler doesn't
     * need to be manually added to the EventsManager where the handler
     * is instantiated. We decided to not include UEventsManager::addHandler(this)
     * in this abstract class constructor because an event can be handled (calling
     * the pure virtual method) while the concrete class is constructed.
     */
    UEventsHandler() {}

    /**
     * UEventsHandler destructor.
     *
     * By default, it removes the handler reference from the UEventsManager. To be thread-safe,
     * the inherited class must remove itself from the UEventsManager before it is deleted because
     * an event can be handled (calling the pure virtual method handleEvent()) after the concrete class
     * is deleted.
     */
    virtual ~UEventsHandler();

private:
    
};
objects.description: Abstract event handler base class exported from the utilite library. It derives from UEventsSender and defines the pure virtual handleEvent(UEvent*) method that UEventsManager calls to dispatch events. Instances should be registered/unregistered with UEventsManager using registerToEventsManager()/unregisterFromEventsManager(). The destructor is virtual and documented to unregister from the manager; however, concrete classes should explicitly unregister before destruction to be thread-safe. Ownership semantics: handleEvent should return true if the handler assumes ownership of the UEvent and will delete it, otherwise return false and UEventsManager deletes it. Threading note: handleEvent is called in UEventsManager's thread; keep work minimal or defer to your own thread if needed.

functions.name: uIsNumber
functions.description: Returns true if str represents a number in either integer form or simple decimal form with one '.' separating integer and fractional parts. Integer part may include a leading '-'; fractional part must be digits only.

functions.name: uSplitNumChar
functions.description: Splits str into alternating numeric and non-numeric substrings. Digits are grouped together; non-digits are grouped together.
requirements: str may be any std::string.
Digits are determined using uIsDigit (ASCII '0'..'9').

functions.name: uStrNumCmp
functions.signature: inline int uStrNumCmp(const std::string & a, const std::string & b)
functions.description: Compares two strings in a human-friendly, alphanumeric way by splitting into digit/non-digit segments. Numeric segments are compared by length (with zero-padding handling) and lexically if same length; non-numeric segments are compared lexically. Returns -1, 0, or 1 for a<b, a==b, a>b respectively.
requirements: Inputs a and b may be any std::string.

functions.name: uStrContains
functions.signature: inline bool uStrContains(const std::string & string, const std::string & substring)
functions.description: Returns true if substring occurs within string (std::string::find != npos).
requirements: Both inputs may be any std::string.
An empty substring returns true.

functions.name: uCompareVersion
functions.signature: inline int uCompareVersion(const std::string & version, int major, int minor = -1, int patch = -1)
functions.description: Compares a version string "X.Y.Z" to provided major/minor/patch integers. Returns 1 if version is greater than the specified (considering only provided components), 0 if equal (treating -1 as wildcard), and -1 otherwise or if version is not exactly three dot-separated components.
requirements: version must contain exactly three dot-separated components; components are parsed with atoi.
minor and patch of -1 act as wildcards when checking equality.
Only strictly greater versions return 1; otherwise returns 0 for match or -1.

functions.name: uPad
functions.signature: inline std::string uPad(const std::string & title, int padding = 20)
functions.description: Right-pads title with spaces to reach the given width. Returns title unchanged if its length is already >= padding.
requirements: padding may be any integer; effective padding occurs only when padding > title.size().
Padding uses ASCII space character ' '.

functions.name: uIsNan
functions.signature: template<class T> inline bool uIsNan(const T & value)
functions.description: Checks whether the given numeric value is NaN. On MSVC uses _isnan; otherwise uses std::isnan. Intended for floating-point types.
requirements: T must be a floating-point compatible type for which isnan/_isnan is valid.
value is passed by const reference.

functions.name: uIsFinite
functions.signature: template<class T> inline bool uIsFinite(const T & value)
functions.description: Checks whether the given numeric value is finite (not NaN or infinity). On MSVC uses _finite; otherwise uses std::isfinite. Intended for floating-point types.
requirements: T must be a floating-point compatible type for which isfinite/_finite is valid.
value is passed by const reference.

functions.name: uMin3
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uMin3(const T & a, const T & b, const T & c)

functions.name: uMax3
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uMax3(const T & a, const T & b, const T & c)
functions.description: Returns the maximum of three values.
requirements: T must support operator> and copy/assignment.

functions.name: uMax
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uMax(const T * v, unsigned int size, unsigned int & index)
functions.description: Returns the maximum value in an array and outputs its index. NaNs are treated as lesser than any non-NaN; a NaN current max will be replaced by a non-NaN element.
requirements: v may be null or size==0; in that case returns T() (initialized as 0 in implementation) and sets index=0.

index must be a valid lvalue reference to receive the position of the max.

functions.name: uMin
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uMin(const T * v, unsigned int size, unsigned int & index)
functions.description: Returns the minimum value in an array and outputs its index. NaNs are treated as greater than any non-NaN; a NaN current min will be replaced by a non-NaN element.
requirements: v may be null or size==0; in that case returns T() (initialized as 0) and sets index=0.
For meaningful results, v must point to at least size valid elements.
T must support operator> and be compatible with uIsNan.
index must be a valid lvalue reference to receive the position of the min.

functions.description: Finds both the minimum and maximum values in an array and outputs their values and indices. NaNs are ignored in comparisons (treated as worse than any non-NaN).
requirements: v may be null or size==0; in that case min/max remain T() (initialized as 0) and indices set to 0.

min, max, indexMin, indexMax must be valid lvalue references for outputs.

functions.name: uSign
functions.signature: template<class T> inline int uSign(const T & v)

requirements: T must support comparison with 0 via operator<.

functions.name: uSum
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uSum(const std::list<T> & list)
functions.description: Sums all values in a std::list and returns the total.
requirements: T must support operator+= and default-initialize to 0-equivalent for accumulation.

functions.name: uSumSquared
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uSumSquared(const T * v, unsigned int size, T subtract = T())
functions.description: Computes the sum of squared values of the array, optionally after subtracting a constant: sum((v[i]-subtract)^2).
requirements: If v is null or size==0, returns T() (initialized as 0).
For meaningful results, v must point to at least size valid elements.
T must support subtraction, multiplication, and accumulation.

functions.name: uMean
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uMean(const T * v, unsigned int size)
functions.description: Computes the arithmetic mean of size elements from the array v. Returns 0-equivalent if input is null or size==0.
requirements: If v is null or size==0, returns T() (initialized as 0).
For meaningful results, v must point to at least size valid elements.
T must support addition and division by an unsigned integer.

functions.name: uMeanSquaredError
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uMeanSquaredError(const T * x, unsigned int sizeX, const T * y, unsigned int sizeY)
functions.description: Computes mean squared error between two arrays: mean((x[i] - y[i])^2). Returns -1 if arrays are null or sizes differ.
requirements: x and y must point to at least sizeX and sizeY valid elements respectively.
Meaningful result requires sizeX == sizeY > 0.
T must support subtraction, multiplication, addition, and division by an unsigned integer.

functions.name: uVariance
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uVariance(const T * v, unsigned int size, T meanV)
functions.description: Computes the sample variance of an array given its mean: sum((v[i]-meanV)^2)/(size-1). Returns 0-equivalent if size <= 1 or v is null.
requirements: v must point to at least size valid elements for size>1.
size must be > 1 for a non-zero result.
T must support subtraction, multiplication, accumulation, and division by an unsigned integer.

functions.name: uNormSquared
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uNormSquared(const std::vector<T> & v)
functions.description: Computes the squared Euclidean norm of a vector: sum(v[i]^2).
requirements: For meaningful results, v.size() > 0.
T must support multiplication, addition, and default initialization to 0-equivalent.

functions.name: uNorm
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T uNorm(const std::vector<T> & v)
functions.description: Computes the Euclidean norm (L2) of a vector: sqrt(sum(v[i]^2)).
requirements: For meaningful results, v.size() > 0.
T must support multiplication, addition, and std::sqrt(T).

functions.name: uNormalize
functions.signature: template<class T> inline std::vector<T> uNormalize(const std::vector<T> & v)
functions.description: Returns a normalized copy of the vector (divide each element by its L2 norm). If norm is 0, returns the original vector unchanged.
requirements: T must support division by a floating-point norm, multiplication, and copy.
For meaningful normalization, vector norm should be non-zero.

functions.name: uLocalMaxima
functions.signature: template<class T> inline std::list<unsigned int> uLocalMaxima(const T * v, unsigned int size)
functions.description: Finds indices of strict local maxima in an array. Endpoints are considered local maxima if they are greater than their single neighbor or if the array has only one element.
requirements: If v is null or size==0, returns an empty list.
For meaningful results, v must point to at least size valid elements.
T must support operator> comparisons.

functions.name: uXMatch
functions.signature: template<class T> inline std::vector<T> uXMatch(const T * vA, const T * vB, unsigned int sizeA, unsigned int sizeB, UXMatchMethod method)
functions.description: Computes the full cross-correlation or cross-covariance between two arrays, producing a vector of length sizeA + sizeB - 1. Methods include raw, biased, unbiased, and coefficient variants for correlation and covariance.
requirements: If vA or vB is null or a size is 0, returns an empty vector.
For meaningful results, vA and vB must point to at least sizeA and sizeB valid elements respectively.
For coefficient methods (UXCorrCoeff, UXCovCoeff), the denominator must be non-zero; inputs with zero variance will cause division by zero.
T must support subtraction, multiplication, addition, division, and std::sqrt on T or a compatible type.

functions.name: uHamming
functions.description: Generates a Hamming window of length L with values in [0,1].
requirements: L specifies the output size. For L==0, returns an empty vector.
Output type is std::vector<float>.

functions.name: uIsInBounds
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline bool uIsInBounds(const T & value, const T & low, const T & high)
functions.description: Checks if value is within [low, high) and finite. Uses uIsFinite(value) and comparisons !(value < low) and !(value >= high).
requirements: T must support comparisons < and >= with itself.
uIsFinite(value) must be valid for type T (intended for arithmetic/floating types).
Bounds define a half-open interval: inclusive of low, exclusive of high.

functions.name: uReplaceChar

All occurrences of character 'before' are replaced by string 'after'.
Function is non-mutating to the input (returns a new std::string).

functions.name: uToUpperCase
functions.description: Returns an uppercased copy of the input string. All alphabetic characters are transformed to uppercase; non-alphabetic characters are left unchanged.

functions.name: uToLowerCase
functions.description: Returns a lowercased copy of the input string. All alphabetic characters are transformed to lowercase; non-alphabetic characters are left unchanged.

functions.name: uNumber2Str

requirements: precision is an integer specifying the number of digits (exact interpretation depends on formatting mode).
fixed selects fixed-point formatting when true.

functions.description: Parses the input string as a base-10 integer and returns its value.
requirements: str should contain a valid decimal integer representation; behavior is unspecified for invalid input (not documented).

functions.description: Parses the input string as a floating-point value independent of locale (handles comma or dot as decimal separator) and returns its float value.
requirements: str should contain a valid floating-point representation; behavior is unspecified for invalid input (not documented).

requirements: str should contain a valid floating-point representation; behavior is unspecified for invalid input (not documented).

functions.description: Converts a boolean to its textual form: "true" or "false".
requirements: Input is any bool.

functions.description: Converts a C-string to a boolean. Returns false if the text is "false", "FALSE", or "0"; returns true for all other inputs.

Case-insensitive only for the word "false" as documented ("FALSE" mentioned); other variants not specified.

functions.description: Converts a std::string to a boolean. Returns false if the text is "false", "FALSE", or "0"; returns true for all other inputs.

functions.name: uStr2Bytes

functions.description: Converts a std::string to a byte array including a trailing null character ("\0").

The returned vector will include a null terminator.

All data before the first '\0' is interpreted as the string content.

bytesLen is the number of bytes to convert.

hex must contain only hexadecimal characters [0-9a-fA-F].

functions.name: uHex2Bytes

functions.description: Converts a buffer containing an even-length hexadecimal string (upper or lower case) to a byte array.

hexLen must be even.
Input must contain only hexadecimal characters [0-9a-fA-F].

functions.description: Converts a hexadecimal string to an ASCII string. The hex string must not contain any 0x00 values ("00"). For binary data containing nulls, use uHex2Bytes instead.
requirements: hex must be even length and contain only hexadecimal characters [0-9a-fA-F].

rightPart selects low nibble when true, high nibble when false.

functions.description: Converts an ASCII hex digit character (0-9, A-F, a-f) to the corresponding 4-bit hexadecimal value in the low nibble.

No ownership transfer is stated; lifetime management of handler remains with the caller.

functions.name: UEventsManager::removeHandler
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added event handler so it no longer receives posted events.
requirements: Handler pointer must refer to a previously added UEventsHandler (removing a non-registered handler is unspecified).
Ensure no concurrent destruction: remove the handler before destroying it to avoid dispatch to a dangling pointer.
Thread-safety: may be called from any thread.

functions.name: UEventsManager::post
functions.signature: static void post(UEvent * event, bool async = true, const UEventsSender * sender = 0);
functions.description: Posts an event to handlers. If async is true, dispatch occurs on UEventsManager’s thread; otherwise the event is dispatched immediately in the caller’s thread (synchronously). Events are automatically deleted after they are posted.
requirements: Event ownership: event is automatically deleted after posting; the caller must not use or delete event after calling post.
Event allocation: event should be dynamically allocated if the caller expects UEventsManager to delete it (inferred from automatic deletion).
Synchronous vs asynchronous: if async is false, handlers are executed in the caller’s thread; callers must be prepared for re-entrant callbacks and potential side effects during the call.
Sender pointer may be null; when non-null it identifies the origin used for pipe filtering.

functions.name: UEventsManager::createPipe
functions.signature: static void createPipe(const UEventsSender * sender, const UEventsHandler * receiver, const std::string & eventName);
functions.description: Creates a directed pipe connecting a specific sender and receiver for a named event. Only receivers connected via appropriate pipes may be targeted, depending on the manager’s dispatching rules.
requirements: Sender and receiver pointers should refer to valid objects when the pipe is created.
eventName must specify the event’s name used for routing (string must be a valid identifier for matching events).
Lifetimes: if either endpoint is destroyed, corresponding pipes should be removed to avoid dangling references (use removePipe/removeAllPipes/removeNullPipes).

functions.name: UEventsManager::removePipe
functions.signature: static void removePipe(const UEventsSender * sender, const UEventsHandler * receiver, const std::string & eventName);
functions.description: Removes a previously created pipe between a sender and receiver for the specified event name.
requirements: The specified pipe should exist; removing a non-existent pipe has unspecified effect.
sender and receiver pointers should reference the same objects used when creating the pipe.
eventName must match the name used at creation.

functions.name: UEventsManager::removeAllPipes
functions.description: Removes all pipes originating from the specified sender, regardless of receiver or event name.
requirements: sender should reference a valid sender whose pipes are to be cleared.
Call before destroying the sender to prevent dangling references.

functions.name: UEventsManager::removeNullPipes
functions.description: Removes any pipes associated with the given sender that have null/invalid endpoints. Useful for cleaning up stale pipe entries.
requirements: sender should reference the sender whose pipes need cleanup.
Exact definition of “null pipes” is not documented; behavior is implementation-dependent.

functions.name: UEventsManager::getInstance
functions.description: Returns the singleton instance of UEventsManager, creating it on first use. Intended for internal and external access to the shared event manager.
requirements: Singleton semantics: only one instance exists application-wide.
Thread-safety: The class is documented as Thread-Safe; getInstance may be called from any thread.

functions.name: UEventsManager::UEventsManager
functions.description: Constructs the UEventsManager singleton. Marked protected so users cannot instantiate directly; created via getInstance.
requirements: Not user-constructible; only the class itself creates the instance (via getInstance).

functions.name: UEventsManager::~UEventsManager
functions.description: Virtual destructor for UEventsManager. Accessible via friend UDestroyer to delete the singleton instance during program shutdown.
requirements: Not user-deletable; destruction is managed by UDestroyer<UEventsManager>.
Ensure no concurrent use during destruction (handled internally by destroyer).

functions.name: UEventsManager::mainLoop
functions.description: Main loop of UEventsManager’s thread. Responsible for waiting on posted events and dispatching them to handlers in FIFO order for asynchronous posting.
requirements: Should be run by the UEventsManager thread only (managed internally).
Callers should not invoke this directly; use post/addHandler interfaces.

functions.name: UEventsManager::mainLoopKill
functions.description: Called to wake up and terminate the UEventsManager thread’s main loop cleanly.
requirements: Internal use only; not intended for external callers.
Must be called in the context of shutting down the manager’s thread.

functions.name: UEventsManager::dispatchEvents
functions.description: Drains and dispatches queued asynchronous events to all relevant handlers in FIFO order.
requirements: Internal use only; relies on internal synchronization over the event queue.
Ordering: preserves FIFO order for asynchronous events.

functions.name: UEventsManager::dispatchEvent
functions.signature: virtual bool dispatchEvent(UEvent * event, const UEventsSender * sender);
functions.description: Dispatches a single event to all relevant handlers, possibly filtered by pipes and event name. Returns a boolean indicating handling status (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: event must point to a valid UEvent for the duration of dispatch.
sender may be null or a valid sender pointer used for pipe filtering.
Return value semantics are not documented; callers should not rely on a specific meaning unless checking the implementation.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_addHandler
functions.description: Internal, non-static implementation of adding an event handler to the manager’s handler list.
requirements: handler must be a valid pointer for the duration it is registered.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_removeHandler
functions.description: Internal, non-static implementation of removing an event handler from the manager’s handler list.
requirements: handler should have been previously added.
Ensure the handler is removed before it is destroyed.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_postEvent
functions.signature: void _postEvent(UEvent * event, bool async = true, const UEventsSender * sender = 0);
functions.description: Internal implementation for posting an event, mirroring the public post API. Handles immediate or queued dispatch and event lifetime management.
requirements: Event ownership: event is deleted after posting; do not access or delete it afterwards.
If async is false, handlers may be invoked synchronously in the caller’s thread.

functions.name: UEventsManager::getPipes
functions.signature: std::list<UEventsHandler*> getPipes(const UEventsSender * sender, const std::string & eventName);
functions.description: Returns the list of handlers that are connected to the specified sender for the given event name via pipes.
requirements: sender should be a valid pointer identifying the source.
eventName specifies the event routing key.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_createPipe
functions.signature: void _createPipe(const UEventsSender * sender, const UEventsHandler * receiver, const std::string & eventName);
functions.description: Internal implementation to create a pipe from sender to receiver for a given event name and store it in the manager’s pipe list.
requirements: sender and receiver must be valid pointers at creation time.
eventName must be the intended routing key.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_removePipe
functions.signature: void _removePipe(const UEventsSender * sender, const UEventsHandler * receiver, const std::string & eventName);
functions.description: Internal implementation to remove a specific pipe identified by sender, receiver, and event name.
requirements: The triplet (sender, receiver, eventName) should match an existing pipe to be removed.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_removeAllPipes
functions.description: Internal implementation to remove all pipes associated with the specified sender.
requirements: sender should refer to the sender whose pipes will be removed.

functions.name: UEventsManager::_removeNullPipes
functions.description: Internal implementation to remove any invalid/null pipes associated with the specified sender.
requirements: sender should refer to the sender whose pipes will be cleaned.
Exact criteria for “null” is not documented; relies on internal definition.

functions.name: UEventsHandler::registerToEventsManager
functions.description: Registers this handler instance with the global UEventsManager so it can start receiving dispatched UEvent objects. Intended as a convenience wrapper around UEventsManager::addHandler(this). Use after the object is fully constructed and before events are expected.
requirements: Must be called only after the derived handler object is fully constructed (do not call from the base-class constructor).
Handler must implement virtual bool handleEvent(UEvent * event).
Should be paired with a later unregisterFromEventsManager() (or rely on the destructor’s automatic removal).
Be aware that handleEvent() will be invoked from the UEventsManager thread; protect shared state accordingly.

functions.name: UEventsHandler::unregisterFromEventsManager
functions.description: Unregisters this handler instance from the UEventsManager so it no longer receives events. Intended as a convenience wrapper around UEventsManager::removeHandler(this). Use before destroying the object to avoid race conditions with in-flight event dispatch.
requirements: Should be called before the handler object is deleted to be thread-safe, as events may otherwise be handled after the concrete class is destroyed.
Safe to call even if already unregistered (exact behavior not specified; typical expectation is idempotence, but not guaranteed by this header).
After unregistering, the instance will no longer receive events; ensure your code does not rely on further event callbacks.

functions.name: UEventsHandler::~UEventsHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor for UEventsHandler. By default, it removes the handler reference from UEventsManager during destruction. However, for thread-safety, derived classes should explicitly unregister themselves before destruction to prevent handleEvent() from being called after object teardown.
requirements: Destructor is virtual; derived classes can override and must ensure base destructor is ultimately invoked.
For thread-safety, callers (or derived classes) must remove/unregister the handler from UEventsManager before object deletion, even though the base destructor also removes it by default.
No arguments and no return value; ensure no events are being handled concurrently during destruction to avoid races (implied by documentation).

functions.name: UEventsSender::UEventsSender
functions.description: Default constructor for UEventsSender. Intended as a base for classes that want to send events via the convenience post() helper that forwards to UEventsManager::post() with this sender. No initialization details are provided in this header.

functions.name: UEventsSender::~UEventsSender
functions.description: Virtual destructor to allow proper cleanup through base pointers for classes deriving from UEventsSender. No specific cleanup behavior is documented here.

functions.name: UEventsSender::post
functions.signature: void post(UEvent * event, bool async = true) const;
functions.description: Convenience method to post an event; equivalent to calling UEventsManager::post() with this sender as the source. Use it from classes that derive from UEventsSender to dispatch events, optionally asynchronously when async is true. Ownership and lifetime semantics of the event are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: Must be called on a valid UEventsSender instance (method is protected; typically invoked from within UEventsSender or its subclasses).
Parameter event must be a valid pointer to a UEvent; behavior for nullptr is unspecified.
The method is const and should not rely on modifying the sender's observable state.
The async parameter controls asynchronous posting when true; exact threading/scheduling behavior is unspecified in this header.
Error handling and return status are not provided; callers should consult UEventsManager::post() documentation for failure modes and requirements.
Event ownership/lifetime and whether the callee deletes or retains the event are not specified; callers must ensure the event remains valid according to UEventsManager::post() expectations.

functions.name: UMutex::UMutex
functions.description: Constructs a UMutex. On POSIX systems, the mutex is initialized as a recursive pthread mutex; on Windows, a CRITICAL_SECTION is initialized. Use with lock()/unlock() to protect shared data. Copy/assignment is disabled for UMutex objects.
requirements: The constructed mutex must remain alive while being used by any thread.
Do not copy or assign UMutex instances (copy constructor and assignment are disabled).
On POSIX, creation relies on pthreads being available and succeeding; callers should be prepared for subsequent lock/unlock calls to return non-zero on errors.

functions.name: UMutex::~UMutex
functions.description: Destroys the mutex. On Windows, deletes the underlying CRITICAL_SECTION. On POSIX, calls pthread_mutex_unlock() then pthread_mutex_destroy() on the underlying mutex. Intended to be called when no threads are using the mutex.
requirements: The mutex should not be held by any thread at destruction time (unlock before destruction) to avoid undefined behavior or errors from the underlying APIs.
Ensure no other threads can attempt to lock/unlock the mutex after destruction.

On POSIX, destroying a locked or unowned mutex is invalid; the destructor unconditionally calls pthread_mutex_unlock() then destroy, so the owning thread must have locked it (if locked) and must unlock it first.

functions.name: UMutex::lock
functions.description: Locks the mutex. If another thread holds the lock, the calling thread blocks until the mutex becomes available. On POSIX builds, the mutex is recursive, so the same thread may lock multiple times without deadlocking.
requirements: Callers must eventually pair each successful lock() with a corresponding unlock() on the same UMutex and from the same thread.
Do not call unlock() without having successfully acquired the lock.
Be aware that lock() may block indefinitely if another thread never releases the mutex.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error code from the underlying platform API (pthread_mutex_lock on POSIX).

functions.name: UMutex::lockTry
functions.description: Attempts to lock the mutex without blocking. If the mutex is already locked by another thread, the call fails immediately. On Windows (when available), returns 0 on success or EBUSY if the lock cannot be acquired. On POSIX, returns the result of pthread_mutex_trylock().
requirements: Callers must pair a successful try-lock (return 0) with a corresponding unlock() from the same thread.

Handle the non-zero return value to detect contention or errors. On Windows, EBUSY indicates the mutex was not acquired; on POSIX, pthread_mutex_trylock return codes apply (e.g., EBUSY if already locked).
Availability: On Windows, lockTry() is only compiled when _WIN32 is defined and _WIN32_WINNT >= 0x0400; otherwise this function may be unavailable.

functions.name: UMutex::unlock
functions.description: Unlocks the mutex previously locked by the calling thread. On success, another waiting thread may acquire the mutex. Returns 0 on success; otherwise returns the underlying platform error code.
requirements: Must be called only by a thread that currently holds the lock on this mutex (and for each prior successful lock).
If the mutex was locked multiple times recursively by the same thread (POSIX), unlock must be called the same number of times to fully release it.
Do not call after the mutex has been destroyed.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error (from LeaveCriticalSection always 0 on Windows per implementation, or pthread_mutex_unlock on POSIX).

functions.name: UScopeMutex::UScopeMutex
functions.description: RAII helper that locks the given UMutex in the constructor and unlocks it in the destructor, ensuring exception-safe and early-return-safe unlocking within a scope.
requirements: The referenced UMutex must remain valid and not be destroyed for the lifetime of this UScopeMutex instance.
The UMutex must be lockable at construction time; construction will call mutex.lock() and may block.
Avoid manual unlocks of the same mutex within the UScopeMutex’s lifetime unless you also manually manage re-locking; UScopeMutex will call unlock() in its destructor.

functions.name: UScopeMutex::~UScopeMutex
functions.description: Destructor that unlocks the associated UMutex acquired in the constructor. Used to automatically release the lock when leaving scope.
requirements: The associated UMutex must still be valid at destruction time.
Do not destroy the UMutex before the UScopeMutex goes out of scope.

functions.name: UObjDeletedEvent::UObjDeletedEvent
functions.description: Constructs a UObjDeletedEvent carrying the deletion thread/object identifier. Typically posted by UObjDeletionThread after it deletes the target object; consumers can read the id via UEvent::getCode().
requirements: objDeletionThreadId may be any valid int; it is used as the event code returned by UEvent::getCode().

functions.name: UObjDeletedEvent::~UObjDeletedEvent
functions.description: Destroys the UObjDeletedEvent instance. No special behavior beyond base-class cleanup is implied.

functions.name: UObjDeletedEvent::getClassName
functions.description: Returns the class name string "UObjDeletedEvent". Useful for runtime identification of the event type.

functions.name: UObjDeletionThread::UObjDeletionThread
functions.signature: template<class T> UObjDeletionThread(T * obj, int id = 0);
functions.description: Constructs a deletion thread object that takes ownership of a dynamically allocated object pointer and will delete it when the thread runs. The provided id is later sent in a UObjDeletedEvent after deletion.
requirements: obj should be a pointer to an object allocated with new that is safe to delete via delete (may be null).
After passing obj to this constructor, the caller must not access or delete the object; ownership is transferred to UObjDeletionThread.
T must have an accessible destructor.

functions.name: UObjDeletionThread::~UObjDeletionThread
functions.description: Joins the worker thread (waiting for deletion to finish if running) and deletes the managed object if it still exists and hasn’t been deleted by the thread yet.
requirements: The caller must not be using the managed object elsewhere; UObjDeletionThread owns and may delete it during destruction.
Destruction may block until the internal thread completes (join).

functions.name: UObjDeletionThread::startDeletion
functions.description: Starts the internal thread to delete the managed object, optionally after a delay. After waitMs milliseconds (if nonzero), the object is deleted, the thread terminates, and a UObjDeletedEvent carrying the configured id is posted.
requirements: waitMs should be a non-negative delay in milliseconds.
Must be called only when a valid object pointer has been set if deletion is expected; calling with a null managed pointer results in no deletion but still posts the event after the wait.
After calling startDeletion, the caller must not access the managed object; it may be deleted asynchronously.

functions.name: UObjDeletionThread::id
functions.description: Returns the identifier associated with this deletion thread instance. This id is included in the UObjDeletedEvent after deletion.

functions.name: UObjDeletionThread::setObj
functions.description: Replaces the managed object. If a previous deletion thread was running, joins it first. Deletes any existing managed object before taking ownership of the new pointer.
requirements: obj should be a pointer to an object allocated with new and safe to delete via delete (may be null).
After passing obj to setObj, the caller must not access or delete it; ownership transfers to UObjDeletionThread.
Call may block to join a previously started internal thread before replacing the object.
T must have an accessible destructor.

functions.name: UProcessInfo::UProcessInfo
functions.description: Default constructor for UProcessInfo. Creates an instance used to query information about the current process. Typically used when you need an object of this class; however, all provided functionality in this header is static, so constructing is optional unless future non-static methods exist.
requirements: No arguments required.
May be called whenever an instance of UProcessInfo is needed.

functions.name: UProcessInfo::~UProcessInfo
functions.description: Virtual destructor for UProcessInfo. Cleans up resources owned by the instance. Provided to allow safe polymorphic deletion if the class is subclassed.
requirements: The object must have been previously constructed before destruction.
If deleting through a base-class pointer, ensure the destructor is invoked (virtual in class definition).

functions.name: UProcessInfo::getMemoryUsage
functions.description: Returns the memory used by the current process in bytes. Intended for monitoring or diagnostics to check how much memory the running process is consuming at the time of the call. Platform-specific behavior and precision are not documented in this header.
requirements: Callable without an instance (static method).
No input arguments required.
Callers should handle the returned long int value as a byte count; overflow behavior or platform-specific limits are unknown.

functions.name: USemaphore::USemaphore
functions.description: Constructs a counting semaphore with an initial count. On Windows, creates a system semaphore with the given initial count and a maximum of SEM_VALUE_MAX. On POSIX, initializes an internal mutex/condition variable and sets the internal count to initValue. Typical usage: create the semaphore with the number of available resources or permits; threads call acquire()/release() to take/return permits.
requirements: Windows: initial count must satisfy 0 <= initValue <= SEM_VALUE_MAX (constraint of CreateSemaphore).
POSIX: no explicit documented bounds in this header; negative values are allowed by implementation (will cause acquire(n) to block until enough releases occur).
The constructor is non-throwing in this header; callers should ensure the environment can create OS synchronization primitives.

functions.name: USemaphore::~USemaphore
functions.description: Destructor that releases underlying OS resources. On Windows, closes the HANDLE. On POSIX, destroys the condition variable and mutex.
requirements: Callers should ensure no other threads are concurrently using or blocked on this semaphore when it is destroyed (common requirement for synchronization objects; not explicitly documented here).

functions.name: USemaphore::acquire
functions.signature: bool USemaphore::acquire(int n = 1, int ms = 0) const
functions.description: Windows variant. Attempts to acquire n permits from the semaphore, blocking up to ms milliseconds. If ms <= 0, waits indefinitely. Returns true on success, false on error/timeout. Each permit is taken via WaitForSingleObject on the underlying HANDLE.
requirements: n is the number of permits to acquire; must be >= 1 for meaningful behavior (inferred from semantics; not explicitly stated).
ms is a timeout in milliseconds; ms <= 0 means infinite wait as documented.
Check the boolean return: false indicates error/timeout; true indicates all n permits acquired.

functions.name: USemaphore::acquireTry
functions.description: Windows variant. Intended to be a non-blocking try-acquire, but the current implementation calls WaitForSingleObject with INFINITE, which blocks. Returns 0 on success, EAGAIN on failure per the code. Note: behavior contradicts the comment that this is non-blocking; treat this as potentially blocking in this implementation.
requirements: Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success; nonzero (EAGAIN) indicates the semaphore could not be acquired without waiting (per intent), though actual call may block.
No parameters.

functions.name: USemaphore::release
functions.description: Windows variant. Releases n permits to the semaphore. Signals waiting threads via ReleaseSemaphore. Returns 0 on success, ERANGE on error.
requirements: n is the number of permits to release; should be >= 1 for meaningful behavior (inferred).
Caller must check return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates error.

functions.name: USemaphore::value
functions.description: Windows variant. Returns the current semaphore count by querying ReleaseSemaphore with a zero increment to fetch the previous count.
requirements: No parameters. Returns the current count as an integer.

functions.name: UThread::currentThreadId
functions.description: Returns the identifier of the calling (current) thread. Intended for logging, debugging, or correlating work to a specific thread. Thread-safe and does not depend on any UThread instance.

functions.name: UThread::UThread
functions.description: Constructs a UThread with the specified priority. The thread is not started by constructing the object; call start() to launch the worker thread. Subclasses typically override mainLoop() (and optionally mainLoopBegin/mainLoopKill/mainLoopEnd).
requirements: The Priority value must be one of: kPLow, kPBelowNormal, kPNormal, kPAboveNormal, kPRealTime.
Subclass must implement mainLoop() (pure virtual).

functions.name: UThread::~UThread
functions.description: Destructor for UThread. Documentation states that inherited classes must call join(true) in their own destructors to avoid leaks if the underlying thread is still running. Not safe to delete a thread while other threads are joining it.
requirements: Derived classes should call join(true) in their destructor to ensure the underlying C-thread is stopped before destruction.
Do not delete a UThread object while other threads are concurrently joining it (not safe).

functions.name: UThread::start
functions.description: Starts the thread and transitions it toward running state. Subsequent calls to start() are ignored until the thread is killed. Affinity and priority (if set) are applied during start. After start, the thread executes mainLoopBegin() once (if overridden) then repeatedly calls mainLoop() until killed.
requirements: Calling start() multiple times while the thread is already started has no effect until the thread is killed.
mainLoop() must be implemented by the subclass (pure virtual requirement).
Do not rely on start() to block; it is non-blocking with respect to thread completion.

functions.name: UThread::kill
functions.description: Requests the thread to stop. Non-blocking. If the thread is not started or is already killed, this is a no-op. When kill is processed, state becomes kSKilled and mainLoopKill() (if overridden) is called to allow releasing waits and avoiding deadlocks.
requirements: : Calling thread must not assume the worker has finished when kill() returns; join() should be used to wait for completion if needed.

functions.name: UThread::join
functions.description: Blocks the caller until the thread finishes. If killFirst is true, kill() is invoked before joining. Intended to coordinate shutdown and guarantee the worker thread has exited before continuing or destroying related resources.
requirements: : Blocking call; the caller must tolerate waiting until the worker exits.
If called from within the worker's own mainLoop(), this may deadlock and is documented as not allowed.
If killFirst is true, the caller must be prepared for any side-effects of kill() (e.g., early termination of in-progress work).

functions.name: UThread::setPriority
functions.description: Sets the thread priority to be applied when the thread starts. If called after start(), documentation implies application occurs during start; behavior of changing priority after start is not specified.
requirements: : Priority must be one of: kPLow, kPBelowNormal, kPNormal, kPAboveNormal, kPRealTime.
Call before start() to ensure the priority is applied during thread creation. Behavior when called after start is not documented.

functions.name: UThread::setAffinity
functions.description: Sets the CPU affinity to be applied during start of the thread. Platform support varies; notes reference macOS and a TODO for Windows. A value of 0 disables affinity (default).
requirements: : cpu must be 0 for no affinity, or a positive CPU id where CPUs are indexed starting at 1.
Affinity is applied during start(); call before start() for effect.
Platform limitations apply (affinity support is platform-dependent; Windows noted as TODO).

functions.name: UThread::isCreating
functions.description: Returns true if the thread state is kSCreating (after start() is called but before entering mainLoop()). Useful to query transitional startup state.

functions.name: UThread::isRunning
functions.description: Returns true if the thread state is kSRunning (executing mainLoop()) or kSCreating. Use to test whether the thread has been started and not yet fully stopped.

functions.name: UThread::isIdle
functions.description: Returns true if the thread state is kSIdle (before start() is called and after the thread is totally killed, or after join(true)).

functions.name: UThread::isKilled
functions.description: Returns true if the thread state is kSKilled (after kill() is called and before the thread is totally killed).

functions.name: UThread::getThreadHandle
functions.description: Returns the underlying thread handle associated with this UThread instance. Intended for advanced/native integration when a platform-specific handle is needed. Validity depends on lifecycle (unknown if non-zero before start).
requirements: : Use only if you understand the underlying threading API represented by Handle.
Caller should not assume the handle is valid before start() or after the thread has fully terminated (exact validity windows are not documented).

functions.name: UThread::getThreadId
functions.description: Returns the thread identifier associated with this UThread instance. Typically set when the thread starts. Useful for diagnostics or correlating logs.
requirements: : Caller should not assume a non-zero/valid id before start() or after full termination (exact guarantees not documented).

functions.name: UTimer::UTimer
functions.description: Constructs a UTimer instance. Initializes internal timestamp/frequency state so the timer can be started and used to measure elapsed time in seconds.

functions.name: UTimer::~UTimer
functions.description: Destroys the UTimer instance. No explicit work is required by callers; resources owned by the timer are released.

functions.name: UTimer::now
functions.description: Returns the current system time in seconds as a double. On Unix it uses gettimeofday(); on Windows it uses QueryPerformanceCounter/Frequency. Intended for obtaining a timestamp independent of a UTimer instance.

functions.name: UTimer::start
functions.description: Starts the timer. Records the current time as the start point for measuring elapsed intervals.

functions.name: UTimer::stop
functions.description: Stops the timer. Records the current time as the stop point so that elapsed() can report a fixed interval between start() and stop().

functions.name: UTimer::elapsed
functions.description: Returns the elapsed time in seconds. If the timer is running, it returns the time between now and the last start(); if the timer has been stopped, it returns the time between stop() and start(). Inline wrapper that forwards to getElapsedTime().
requirements: Call start() at least once before relying on the returned value to represent a meaningful interval.

functions.name: UTimer::getElapsedTime
functions.description: Returns the elapsed time in seconds. If the timer is running, it measures from the last start() to now; if the timer is stopped, it returns the interval between stop() and start().
requirements: Call start() at least once before relying on the returned value to represent a meaningful interval.

functions.name: UTimer::getInterval
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the interval in seconds between stop() and start(). Use elapsed() instead.
requirements: Call start() and then stop() to define a valid interval for this method to report.
Prefer using elapsed() as this method is deprecated.

functions.name: UTimer::restart
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper for ticks(). Stops the timer if running, returns the measured interval in seconds, and restarts the timer, allowing consecutive interval measurements.
requirements: Call start() at least once before the first restart() if you want the first returned interval to be meaningful.

functions.name: UTimer::ticks
functions.description: Stops the timer, returns the elapsed interval in seconds, and restarts the timer. Equivalent to calling stop(), elapsed(), then start(). Useful for periodic timing/benchmarking loops.
requirements: Call start() at least once before the first ticks() if you want the first returned interval to be meaningful.

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets an arbitrary string input used across many stubs.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, interesting strings that exercise different code paths:
#   * empty, short, and long strings
#   * numeric-looking (integers, floats, versions)
#   * hex strings (even length, valid chars; with/without 00 pairs)
#   * path-like strings and file-like names with extensions
#   * mixed alnum/non-alnum for split/compare routines
#   * characters covering ASCII classes
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_LEN = 1024  # keep well under 4096 to be safe across multiple consumers

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
HEX_UP = string.digits + "ABCDEF"
HEX_LO = string.digits + "abcdef"
PRINTABLE = string.printable.replace("\x0b", "").replace("\x0c", "")


def _rand(r: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return r.randrange(lo, hi + 1)


def _make_integer(r: random.Random) -> str:
    n_digits = _rand(r, 1, 18)
    sign = '-' if r.random() < 0.3 else ''
    digits = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n_digits))
    # avoid leading zero-only like "-0" with many zeros; keep as-is otherwise valid
    return sign + digits


def _make_float(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # locale-independent float using '.' or ',' as decimal sep
    n_int = _rand(r, 1, 8)
    n_frac = _rand(r, 1, 8)
    sign = '-' if r.random() < 0.3 else ''
    sep = '.' if r.random() < 0.5 else ','
    left = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n_int))
    right = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n_frac))
    return f"{sign}{left}{sep}{right}"


def _make_version(r: random.Random) -> str:
    a = str(_rand(r, 0, 100000))
    b = str(_rand(r, 0, 100000))
    c = str(_rand(r, 0, 100000))
    return f"{a}.{b}.{c}"


def _make_hex_even(r: random.Random, upper: bool = True, allow_00: bool = True) -> str:
    n_bytes = _rand(r, 1, 64)
    alpha = HEX_UP if upper else HEX_LO
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alpha) for _ in range(n_bytes * 2))
    if not allow_00:
        # replace any "00" pairs
        lst = list(s)
        for i in range(0, len(lst), 2):
            if lst[i] == '0' and lst[i+1] == '0':
                lst[i+1] = '1'
        s = ''.join(lst)
    return s


def _make_path_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create simple relative or absolute-ish paths
    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = _rand(r, 1, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name_len = _rand(r, 1, 8)
        name = ''.join(r.choice(ALNUM + "_- ") for _ in range(name_len)).strip()
        if not name:
            name = 'x'
        parts.append(name)
    prefix = ''
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        prefix = '/'
    return prefix + '/'.join(parts)


def _make_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    stem_len = _rand(r, 1, 12)
    stem = ''.join(r.choice(ALNUM + "_- ") for _ in range(stem_len)).strip()
    if not stem:
        stem = 'file'
    exts = ['txt', 'log', 'jpg', 'bmp', 'png', 'dat']
    ext = r.choice(exts)
    return f"{stem}.{ext}"


def _make_mixed(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Alternating digit and non-digit runs to exercise split/compare
    runs = _rand(r, 2, 8)
    out = []
    digit_run = r.random() < 0.5
    for _ in range(runs):
        ln = _rand(r, 1, 6)
        if digit_run:
            out.append(''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(ln)))
        else:
            pool = (string.ascii_letters + "_-.:/ ")
            out.append(''.join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(ln)))
        digit_run = not digit_run
    return ''.join(out)


def _make_random_printable(r: random.Random) -> str:
    ln = _rand(r, 0, 256)
    return ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(ln))


def _make_case_mix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of cases for uToUpperCase/uToLowerCase
    ln = _rand(r, 1, 128)
    out = []
    for _ in range(ln):
        k = r.random()
        if k < 0.4:
            out.append(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase))
        elif k < 0.8:
            out.append(r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase))
        else:
            out.append(r.choice(string.digits))
    return ''.join(out)


def _make_ext_filter(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # space-separated extensions for UDirectory filters
    choices = ["", "txt", "jpg bmp", "png jpg", "dat log txt"]
    return r.choice(choices)


def _assemble_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands = []
    # Prioritize a diverse set
    cands.append("")  # empty
    cands.append(" ")  # single space
    cands.append("-")  # lone sign
    cands.append(_make_integer(r))
    cands.append(_make_float(r))
    cands.append(_make_version(r))
    cands.append(_make_hex_even(r, upper=True, allow_00=True))
    cands.append(_make_hex_even(r, upper=False, allow_00=False))
    cands.append(_make_path_like(r))
    cands.append(_make_filename(r))
    cands.append(_make_mixed(r))
    cands.append(_make_random_printable(r))
    cands.append(_make_case_mix(r))
    cands.append(_make_ext_filter(r))
    # Join parts to exercise uJoin and long strings while staying within limit
    parts = [ _make_random_printable(r)[:_rand(r,0,16)] for _ in range(_rand(r,2,6)) ]
    sep = r.choice(["", ",", ":", "/", "|"])
    cands.append(sep.join(parts))
    # Pad candidate to test uPad
    title = _make_random_printable(r)[:_rand(r,0,20)]
    pad_width = _rand(r, 0, 40)
    if len(title) < pad_width:
        cands.append(title + (" " * (pad_width - len(title))))
    else:
        cands.append(title)
    # Ensure we have at least one that looks like a real directory token
    cands.append("ctor_token")
    return cands


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a list of interesting candidates and pick several to concatenate
    cands = _assemble_candidates(r)

    # Randomly select how many segments to pack; ensure we keep under MAX_LEN
    out_segments: List[str] = []
    total_len = 0
    # Use a header to lightly guide consumers that may read multiple strings sequentially
    # Format: count N (1 byte), then N segments each prefixed by 2-byte big-endian length and UTF-8 bytes.
    # This keeps input self-describing while still being plain bytes for arbitrary-string consumers.
    selected = r.sample(cands, k=min(len(cands), _rand(r, 3, 10)))

    payload = bytearray()
    payload.append(len(selected) & 0xFF)
    for s in selected:
        # Occasionally transform to uppercase/lowercase to vary content
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.1:
            s = s.upper()
        elif t < 0.2:
            s = s.lower()
        # Trim to stay within limits
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 256:
            b = b[:256]
        if len(payload) + 2 + len(b) > MAX_LEN:
            break
        payload += struct.pack('>H', len(b))
        payload += b
        out_segments.append(s)

    # If nothing added (extreme corner), add a small safe default
    if len(payload) <= 1:
        s = "0"
        b = s.encode('utf-8')
        payload.append(1)
        payload += struct.pack('>H', len(b)) + b

    return bytes(payload)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets APIs that consume arbitrary file paths and filenames.
# The fuzzing harness provides FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() as an existing, writable file
# path populated with random data. Our buffer should therefore contain a single
# path string that the harness will use to create such a file. We will generate
# a relative path (possibly nested) that is valid on POSIX and Windows and short
# enough to avoid path length issues. We include a plausible filename with or
# without an extension, and optional subdirectories the harness can create.
#
# The stubs also call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for directory names and miscellaneous
# strings. To seed those with interesting but valid values, we embed alphanumeric
# chunks and a few separators.
#
# Contract: return bytes buffer <= 4096 containing text the fuzzer runtime
# interprets to create files. We avoid exotic characters and reserved device
# names; we ensure the leaf is a filename, not a directory.

SAFE_ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS = SAFE_ALNUM + "-_ ."
SAFE_DIRNAME_CHARS = SAFE_ALNUM + "-_"

EXTS = [
    "txt", "log", "dat", "bin", "cfg", "json", "xml", "csv", "tmp",
    ""  # allow no extension sometimes
]


def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, n_min: int = 3, n_max: int = 10, chars: str = SAFE_ALNUM) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(n_min, n_max)
    return "".join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_dirname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # avoid names that are reserved on Windows
    reserved = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL"} | {f"COM{i}" for i in range(1, 10)} | {f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1, 10)}
    while True:
        name = _rand_token(rng, 3, 12, SAFE_DIRNAME_CHARS)
        if name.upper() not in reserved:
            return name


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # base name
    base = _rand_token(rng, 4, 16, SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS).strip()
    base = base.replace(" ", "_")
    # ensure not empty and not dot-only
    if not base or set(base) == {'.'}:
        base = _rand_token(rng, 6, 10, SAFE_ALNUM)
    # choose extension
    ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    if ext:
        # ensure base has no trailing dot duplication
        base = base.rstrip('.')
        return f"{base}.{ext}"
    else:
        # no extension
        base = base.strip('.')
        if not base:
            base = _rand_token(rng, 6, 10, SAFE_ALNUM)
        return base


def _build_relative_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 0-3 nested directories to exercise UDirectory paths.
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_dirname(rng))
    parts.append(_rand_filename(rng))  # leaf is a file
    # Use forward slashes; most C++ code accepts them even on Windows.
    return "/".join(parts)


def _interesting_variants(rng: random.Random, rel: str) -> List[str]:
    # Produce a small set of path variants for the harness to consume across calls:
    # - plain relative
    # - prefixed with ./
    # - include a sibling directory traversal (still safe/relative)
    # - add numeric-heavy name
    variants = [rel]
    if not rel.startswith("./"):
        variants.append("./" + rel)
    # Add a traversal variant but keep within relative scope
    filename = os.path.basename(rel)
    variants.append("sub/..//" + filename)
    # numeric heavy alternative
    num = _rand_token(rng, 6, 12, string.digits)
    ext = rng.choice(["txt", "bin", "log"])  # keep simple
    variants.append(f"{_rand_dirname(rng)}/{num}.{ext}")
    # ensure uniqueness and length limits
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for v in variants:
        v = v.strip()
        if not v:
            continue
        if len(v) > 240:  # keep short per component
            v = v[:240]
        if v not in seen:
            seen.add(v)
            uniq.append(v)
    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rel = _build_relative_path(rng)
    paths = _interesting_variants(rng, rel)

    # Join variants with newlines so the harness can consume multiple filenames
    # if it splits the buffer for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() invocations.
    # Also include a couple of generic tokens that FUZZ_PARAM_STR() might pick up.
    tokens = [
        _rand_token(rng, 5, 12, SAFE_ALNUM),
        _rand_token(rng, 3, 8, SAFE_ALNUM),
    ]

    # Compose buffer: first lines are file paths, then some generic strings.
    lines: List[str] = []
    lines.extend(paths)
    lines.extend(tokens)

    data = ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
